head: 80e114a6f0eac29cfdce0d64d455563fe87b5113
summary:
HF-009 is fixed as the design describes. Scans.WithGuard (Scans.cs:111-122) and Scans.RunCancellingAt (Scans.cs:129-153) now hold the Created set/reset and the cancel-at-call-k arming. CancelledFolderTests.CancelAtAnyCallCommitsOnlyWholeFolders (:44, :67) and TopLevelTests.CancelAtAnyCallLeavesAFinalSnapshotThatAddsUpToTheTotals (:269, :276) call both helpers for the baseline scan and for every cancelled scan. I read the diff against the old code and found the behaviour unchanged. Each run still gets its own CTS, created before Created is set. BeforeCall cancels at call k. AfterCall cancels at call k and then spins on CancelIsIssued with the same message. Created is reset in a finally. The call number is captured as a parameter, where the old code copied it into a local (cancelAt). One difference: the CTS is now disposed as soon as the scan returns, not at the end of each loop iteration. That is safe, because the guard is disposed inside Scan, which removes its registration and drains its cancel attempts, and neither ScanResult nor Watched keeps the token. I re-ran the full default suite myself: 394 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, in 24 s. Every fitness rule holds (62 checked). Only one build attempt was made, so the slice is not looping. One minor finding: the new helper is now a third copy of arming code the tree already had, and one of the older copies has already diverged from the others. The builder's leftover list (CancellationTests, StalledShareTests, CloudRig/CloudPlaceholder, TopLevelRowText) is accurate, apart from stale line numbers for CancelledFolderTests. Those sites are now at :200 and :215, not :239/:254. The design listed no case matrix, so there were no cases to check.

Second round: Round two found nothing new. This diff adds no parser, matcher or reader. I tried to break the two new helpers from both sides.

- **Caller side:** Both callers pass call numbers from 1 up to the number of calls in the baseline scan. A call number outside that range never arms anything, so the scan completes and the caller's Cancelled assert fails loudly rather than passing silently.
- **Callee side:** An assert thrown inside AfterCall, or any exception from the scan, still reaches the finally that clears Created, and the CTS is still disposed on that path. The run-local progress object is captured fresh on each loop iteration.
- **CTS disposed earlier:** The CTS is now disposed right after Scan returns. By then the guard has already removed its registration and drained its cancel attempts, and the token is not held by the result or by the Watched record.
- **Thread-static seam:** It behaves as before. Created runs on the scan thread, and the probe workers never see it.
- **Nesting:** WithGuard clears Created to null rather than restoring an earlier value. No caller nests it, so nothing breaks today.

I ran the five CancelledFolderTests tests and the TopLevelTests cancel-at-call-k theory (8 test cases) five times in a row: 8/8 passed every time, 6–7 s per run. The first-round minor finding m1 still stands, and I have not filed it again.

findings.claim: Scans.RunCancellingAt's during-the-call branch is the third copy of 'cts.Cancel(); spin until CancelIsIssued, "the canceller never marked the call"'. SynchronousIoCancelTests already has this as a private helper, CancelDuringTheCall(cts, guard). CancelledFolderTests.AnAbortedListingKeepsNothingOfTheBuffersBeforeIt, in a file this diff touched, still has its own copy of the whole before/during arming block (AfterCall with Cancel and the spin, or BeforeCall with Cancel, at call k). That copy has already drifted: its SpinUntil assert carries no message. HF-009 was about exactly this, copies of this machinery drifting in an area with a known flaky suite (SC-034), and the design says to 'Keep one helper'. The two tests named in the finding now share code, but the arming itself still exists in three places.
findings.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/Scans.cs:134-151 (new). tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/SynchronousIoCancelTests.cs:376-380, private static void CancelDuringTheCall(CancellationTokenSource cts, SynchronousIoCancel guard), with the identical message. tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/CancelledFolderTests.cs:123-140, the same if (duringTheCall) { guard.AfterCall = … cts.Cancel(); Assert.True(SpinWait.SpinUntil(() => guard.CancelIsIssued, …)) } else { guard.BeforeCall = … cts.Cancel() }, with no message on the assert.
findings.fix: Move the arming out of RunCancellingAt into `internal static void Scans.CancelAt(SynchronousIoCancel g, CancellationTokenSource cts, int call, bool during)`. RunCancellingAt then becomes WithGuard(g => CancelAt(g, cts, call, during), …). Call CancelAt from AnAbortedListingKeepsNothingOfTheBuffersBeforeIt (CancelledFolderTests.cs:123-140). Replace SynchronousIoCancelTests.CancelDuringTheCall with a single shared Scans method that both files call.

obligations.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/Scans.cs:107-153 adds WithGuard<T>(Action<SynchronousIoCancel>, Func<T>), which sets Created, runs the scan and resets Created in a finally, and RunCancellingAt<T>(root, call, during, Func<string, CancellationToken, T>), which owns the CTS and arms BeforeCall, or AfterCall plus the CancelIsIssued spin. CancelledFolderTests.cs:44 and :67, and TopLevelTests.cs:269 and :276, call them. Neither test still has its own copy of the loop body or of the Created set/reset. Full suite re-run by this review: 394/394 passed.

drift: No undeclared departure from the design. The builder said it left the other SynchronousIoCancel.Created set/reset sites alone (CancellationTests.cs:80/203/258, CancelledFolderTests.cs:200/215, StalledShareTests.cs:54, CloudPlaceholderTests.cs:374, CloudRigTests.cs:192/237, TopLevelRowTextTests.cs:70). Its follow-up cites the CancelledFolderTests sites as :239/:254, which are line numbers from before the change. In the tree they are now :200 and :215.

No new departure from the design. From round one: the builder's follow-up still gives CancelledFolderTests.cs:239/254 for the remaining Created sites, which were the line numbers before the change. In the tree they are now :200 and :215.
